lint.reason: next lint prompts to configure ESLint

summary.mainProblem: The project is split between profile-based workers and the new workers table model.

findings.title: Two worker models are active at the same time
findings.details: Old code uses profiles.role=worker and tickets.assigned_to. New workers module uses workers and tickets.assignee_worker_id. Permissions, RLS, reports, and UI do not consistently use the same model.
evidence: lib/auth/permissions.ts uses assigned_to for worker permissions
lib/supabase/queries.ts filters worker tickets by assigned_to
tickets table contains both assigned_to and assignee_worker_id
findings.impact: Workers may not see tickets assigned through the new module; reports may be wrong; RLS may block or expose wrong data.
findings.recommendation: Choose one canonical worker model and migrate permissions, RLS, reports, queries, and UI to it.

findings.title: Pending review confirmation has duplicated business logic
findings.details: AI-ticket confirmation and ticket-detail confirmation perform different transitions.
evidence: app/(app)/ai-tickets/actions.ts confirmAiTicketAction may assign worker and send Telegram
app/(app)/tickets/[id]/actions.ts confirmTicketAction changes pending_review to new
findings.impact: The same ticket can follow different lifecycle paths depending on which page is used.
findings.recommendation: Create a shared ticket lifecycle service for confirming, rejecting, assigning, and sending worker notifications.

findings.title: Permissions and RLS still use the old assigned_to model
findings.details: Worker access in application permissions and Supabase policies is still tied to tickets.assigned_to/auth.uid(), while the new module assigns tickets through assignee_worker_id.
evidence: RLS policies from migrations use assigned_to = auth.uid()
findings.impact: Assigned workers in the new workers table may not have correct access.
findings.recommendation: Define relation between workers and auth profiles or treat workers as Telegram-only executors, then update RLS accordingly.

findings.title: Telegram worker callback may be running old deployed code
findings.details: Local code routes wd:* callback_query before message handling, but the reported Telegram behavior matches the legacy dialog fallback.
evidence: lib/telegram/handlers.ts contains legacy stale action response
User observed stale action text after pressing worker Done button
findings.impact: Production Telegram may keep failing even when local branch is fixed.
findings.recommendation: Verify Telegram getWebhookInfo, Vercel deployment branch and commit, and redeploy the exact feature/workers-module commit.

findings.title: Reports are not adapted to the new workers module
findings.details: Worker analytics still rely on profiles and assigned_to instead of workers and assignee_worker_id.
findings.impact: Excel reports can show incorrect performer statistics.
findings.recommendation: Update report queries and aggregation to use assignee_worker_id and workers table.

findings.title: Webhook documentation does not match implementation
findings.details: The route checks query param ?secret=, while documentation mentions Telegram secret_token/header.
findings.impact: Webhook can be installed with the wrong secret mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Update README and deployment notes to one supported method.

findings.title: sendTicketToWorker has hidden assignment side effects
findings.details: Sending Telegram can also update ticket assignment/status if the selected worker differs.
findings.impact: A notification action can mutate core ticket ownership unexpectedly.

findings.title: Status naming is inconsistent
findings.details: Some code mentions completed while the ticket enum uses done as final completion status.
findings.impact: Filters and statistics may misclassify completed work.
findings.recommendation: Use one canonical completed status, preferably the DB enum value.

findings.title: Workers route is not fully represented in mobile navigation
findings.details: Desktop sidebar includes /workers, but mobile navigation does not fully expose it.
findings.impact: Mobile users may not find the workers module.

findings.title: ESLint is not configured for non-interactive CI
findings.details: npm run lint launches next lint setup prompt.
findings.impact: CI cannot reliably lint without manual input.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit ESLint config or update lint script.

telegram.deploymentRisk: If stale action appears in Telegram, webhook likely points to old Vercel deployment or wrong branch.

ai.risk: Object resolver candidate selection should be checked for ambiguous/not_found cases.

database.mainConcern: RLS policies still depend on assigned_to while new worker assignments use assignee_worker_id.

recommendedFixOrder: Verify Telegram webhook URL, branch, deployment SHA, and query secret mode.
Decide canonical worker model: profiles/assigned_to or workers/assignee_worker_id.
Move ticket lifecycle transitions into shared server-side services.
Update permissions and RLS to match the canonical worker model.
Unify pending_review confirmation behavior across /ai-tickets and /tickets/[id].
Update reports to use the new worker assignment model.
Clean up webhook docs, lint config, and mobile navigation.
